description: OpenAirClim is a Python response model from the German Aerospace Center for estimating climate effects of air-traffic emissions. It applies response functions derived from larger climate-chemistry models instead of running those physical models for each flight scenario. Users supply emission amounts, species, location and time information, together with response-model settings; outputs are climate-impact indicators for an aviation traffic scenario. Geographic coverage follows the flight and emission inputs, potentially beyond one airport. Apache-2.0 source, PyPI and conda packages, detailed documentation and code and data DOIs are public. A limitation is that response functions approximate a more complex climate system, so results depend on their domain, species and metric choices. OpenAirClim can compare aviation demand or route options for airport and airspace planning. The related catalogue AEOLUS Dutch aviation forecast models traffic demand, not emission climate response. A separate G7 CLIMaCCF draft addresses another method and is not linked as an existing catalogue record. No flight data or package was downloaded.
